cards.heading: Start embarrassingly small
cards.body: The biggest mistake when building new habits is starting too big. A 1-minute walk beats a 5km run you never do. Tiny habits build identity. You're becoming 'someone who moves every day' — not 'trying to exercise'.

cards.question: Why do small habits succeed more often than ambitious ones?

options.text: Small habits require less willpower to start
Your brain can't handle large changes
Small habits are easier to track

cards.explanation: Getting started is the hardest part. A habit you actually do beats a perfect habit you don't. Once started, you usually do more than planned.

cards.heading: The compound effect
cards.body: Small consistent actions compound dramatically. 30 minutes of exercise a day seems small, but over 30 days that's 15 hours of movement you wouldn't have had. The habit isn't the action — it's the identity it builds.

cards.statement: Missing one day of a new habit breaks your progress and you should start over.
cards.explanation: Missing one day has almost no effect on a habit. The real risk is missing two days in a row — that's when habits break. The rule is: never miss twice.

cards.heading: The 'never miss twice' rule
cards.body: If you miss a day, your only job is to show up the next day. One miss is an accident. Two misses is the start of a new habit — in the wrong direction.

cards.prompt: Pick one new habit to start this week. Make it so small it feels almost too easy. What is it, and when exactly will you do it? (Specific time + existing habit to stack it on.)
